result.title: Big Models, Small Gains: Frozen Forecasters as Classifiers on MONSTER
result.comment: Asian Conference on Machine Learning, FMLTS Workshop, 2026
result.summary: Forecasting foundation models are increasingly used as frozen feature extractors for time series classification, but it remains unclear whether their pretrained representations offer an advantage over strong classifiers that do not require pretraining. This raises an important question: do these representations provide useful information beyond what the model architecture alone can capture, particularly when labelled data are scarce? We present a controlled benchmarking of two forecasting models, Reverso and Chronos-Bolt, on six large datasets from the MONSTER benchmark, using 1%, 10%, and 100% of the available training labels. We compare their frozen representations against four established time series classification methods and random-weight versions of the same forecasting models. Our results show that pretraining improves classification accuracy over random-weight counterparts on five of the six datasets, with gains of up to 23 percentage points. However, the frozen representations do not reliably outperform the strongest non-pretrained baseline in any setting: they perform worse in 15 of 17 settings and tie in the remaining two. Further experiments show that restoring amplitude information recovers part of the performance gap, while fine-tuning and forecast-error features do not close it. These findings highlight the importance of strong task specific baselines and random weight controls when evaluating forecasting foundation models for classification. Our code is available at https://github.com/Rachet2006/frozen-forecasters-monster.

AI.brief_summary: 在 MONSTER 的六个大规模时序分类数据集上，以 1%、10%、100% 标签比例比较两个 forecasting 基础模型（Reverso、Chronos-Bolt）的冻结表示与四种成熟分类器及同架构随机权重版本，发现预训练相对随机权重多数有效，但仍稳定弱于最强非预训练基线。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「随机权重对照＋强任务基线」的表示评估范式可能可供核查：用于判断 VLM latent 状态中保留的任务信息究竟来自预训练还是架构本身；但论文属时序领域，迁移到视觉多模态推理需较多验证。
